purpose: Reassess unresolved ownership overlaps between 600-series and active lanes, classified per S601 findings. Determine which conflicts block activation, which are procedural, and which carry forward.
evidence_sources: S600 Reserve Charter v1.0 §2.2 (IS NOT prohibitions), §3 (Ownership Boundaries)
S601 Ownership Boundary Audit (Agent B, 95/100 integrity score)
S601 Activation Gate Review (Agent E, 2 MEDIUM overlaps)
S601 Agent F Conflict Simulation (3 violation scenarios)
S725 Post-700 Governance Model §5 (6 ownership gaps, GAP-3 = 600 deferral)
S726 Ownership Acceptance Registry (0 of 6 accepted)
S727 Ownership Acceptance Status (GAP-3 = PENDING, deadline passed)

classification_framework.OPEN: Conflict is unresolved and actively blocking a governance gate. Requires remediation before the associated lane milestone (activation, certification, etc.).
classification_framework.ACCEPTED: Conflict is acknowledged but accepted as non-blocking. Both affected lanes have documented the overlap and agreed it does not impair lane operations. No remediation required.
classification_framework.CARRY_FORWARD: Conflict is documented and understood but cannot be resolved in the current lane state (e.g., 600 is DEFERRED). Must be addressed during the first activation wave if and when activation occurs. Not blocking the current DEFERRED state.

c_001_800_handoff_friction.description: 600 charter §3.3 authorizes drafting support for 800 certification passes. The 600→800 handoff boundary (draft acceptance, rejection, revision cycles) has no operational specification. In practice, drafts may be rejected at 80%+ rate (S601 Agent G assumption) with no standardized rejection workflow. This could create friction where 600-authored drafts add overhead to 800 certification passes rather than reducing it.
c_001_800_handoff_friction.dormant_state_impact: None. While 600 is DEFERRED, no handoff occurs. C-001 only manifests during activation.
c_001_800_handoff_friction.classification_rationale: Cannot be resolved while 600 is dormant because: (1) handoff specification requires bilateral negotiation between 600 and 800 agents, neither of which is active. (2) The 800-series certification pipeline is the active bottleneck definition — until throughput data exists, rejection rates are purely speculative. (3) CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification is the binding quality gate regardless of who authored the draft. Resolution must occur during activation review as part of GATE_OWNERSHIP satisfaction.
c_001_800_handoff_friction.resolution_plan_when_activated: During activation review: 800-series Certification Lead and 600-series Draft Preparation Lead must jointly define: (1) draft acceptance criteria (minimum quality bar), (2) rejection workflow and revision cycle SLA, (3) escalation path for disputed drafts, (4) acceptance-rate monitoring and calibration cadence. A new S725 Ownership Matrix row (Row 26+) must reflect this handoff specification.
c_001_800_handoff_friction.blocking_rationale: GATE_OWNERSHIP (S600 Charter §5.3) requires all ownership conflicts resolved before activation. C-001 must be resolved.

c_002_700_authority_drift.description: 600 charter §2.1 authorizes standards library maintenance (explanation templates, distractor templates, feedback templates). 700-series owns governance standards (CAQS v1.0, DCS, enforcement rules). The boundary between 'template library' (600 domain) and 'governance standard' (700 domain) is undefined. A template that becomes de facto mandatory through widespread adoption by 800-series authors would have the force of a governance standard without 700 authorization. Conversely, 700 could categorically reject all 600 templates, defeating their purpose.
c_002_700_authority_drift.dormant_state_impact: None. While 600 is DEFERRED, no templates exist to create this tension.
c_002_700_authority_drift.classification_rationale: Cannot be resolved while 600 is dormant because: (1) template library content does not yet exist — the tension is at the boundary design level. (2) 700-series governance standards are currently defined at the conceptual level (CAQS, DCS) without operational template specifications. (3) The boundary is resolvable through a joint rubric requiring 700 review and approval of all 600-produced templates before 800 adoption. Resolution must occur during activation review as part of GATE_OWNERSHIP satisfaction.
c_002_700_authority_drift.resolution_plan_when_activated: During activation review: 700-series Governance Auditor and 600-series Standards Library Maintainer must jointly define: (1) a template classification rubric distinguishing 'non-binding reference template' from 'governance-mandated standard,' (2) a 700-review gate for all templates before release to 800, (3) a deprecation protocol for outdated templates. A new S725 Ownership Matrix row (Row 27+) must reflect the template governance boundary.
c_002_700_authority_drift.blocking_rationale: GATE_OWNERSHIP (S600 Charter §5.3) requires all ownership conflicts resolved before activation. C-002 must be resolved.

c_003_registry_maintenance_tension.description: S600 Charter §4.1 authorizes Agent A to maintain MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md. AGENTS.md Rule 3 states the registry is generated by script — never hand-edited. S601 Agent B flagged this as a LOW procedural tension. S601 Agent C identified that build_master_registry.js and generate_registry.js already produce the registry without 600 involvement.
c_003_registry_maintenance_tension.dormant_state_impact: None. Registry maintenance is currently handled by build scripts (no human agent edits).
c_003_registry_maintenance_tension.s601_status: Identified by Agent B — not yet classified.
c_003_registry_maintenance_tension.classification_rationale: This is a procedural note, not a blocking conflict. The charter's 'maintenance' language is intentionally broad. Three resolution paths exist: (1) restrict 600 Agent A to similarity ledger and registry index artifacts (not the master registry), preserving AGENTS.md Rule 3, (2) transfer build-script ownership to 600 (adds operational overhead for marginal benefit), or (3) accept the tension — 600 maintains non-code-generated artifacts; build scripts maintain the master registry. Path 1 is the recommended resolution. Not blocking because: (a) it is LOW severity, (b) the registry already exists without 600, and (c) the build scripts handle actual maintenance.
c_003_registry_maintenance_tension.resolution: During activation: define the S600 Agent A scope as 'QUESTION_SIMILARITY_LEDGER.json + QUESTION_REGISTRY_INDEX.md' (non-master artifacts). MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md remains build-script-generated per AGENTS.md Rule 3.

c_004_analytics_consumption_boundary.description: S600 Charter §3.1 authorizes 600 to 'consume 300-series outputs' and 'report throughput metrics upstream to 300.' S601 Agent C identified this as a cross-lane data flow where 600 registry stats feed 300 quality models. The consumption boundary is defined at the design level ('600 may consume, may not produce competing analytics') but has no operational specification for what consumption looks like.
c_004_analytics_consumption_boundary.dormant_state_impact: None. No consumption occurs while 600 is DEFERRED.
c_004_analytics_consumption_boundary.s601_status: Identified by Agent C (registry bleeds into analytics). Not classified.
c_004_analytics_consumption_boundary.classification_rationale: The consumption vs. production boundary is well-defined in the charter: 600 reads 300 outputs but never modifies 300 models or produces competing metrics. This is the standard producer/consumer pattern across all lanes. The boundary does not need further specification because: (a) the charter explicitly prohibits 600 from producing analytics, (b) the 300-series models are read-only for all non-300 lanes, and (c) the governance guard has no visibility into 600 analytics-consumption behavior — the prohibition is procedural (Agent F Scenario 1 confirms this).

c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.description: S725 Row 16 assigns 600-series stewardship to the Governance Board. Per Stewardship Principle 2, 'ownership cannot be transferred by assignment alone — the receiving party must explicitly accept.' The Governance Board has not accepted GAP-3 (0/6 acceptances as of S727). This is a design-level ownership gap, not an operational conflict, but it blocks GATE_BOARD satisfaction because the entity that would hold the activation vote has not accepted stewardship of the lane.
c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.dormant_state_impact: Creates an orphaned lane with no accountable owner. The dormancy controls prevent operational impact, but the ownership gap undermines the governance framework.
c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.s601_status: Flagged as GAP-3 PENDING by S601 Agent I (Stewardship Dashboard).
c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.classification_rationale: This is not a 600-series operational issue — it is a governance process issue affecting all 6 deferred gaps. However, GATE_BOARD requires a Governance Board vote for activation, and the Governance Board has not accepted ownership. Until acceptance occurs, there is no authorized entity to hold the vote. This blocks activation and creates governance debt that must be resolved. Unlike C-001/C-002 (which are CARRY_FORWARD because they require bilateral negotiation between inactive lanes), C-005 can be resolved NOW by Governance Board acceptance — no 600-series agent is needed.
c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.resolution_plan: The Governance Board must explicitly accept S725 Row 16 stewardship per Stewardship Principle 2. Acceptance requires: (1) named primary steward (Governance Board member), (2) documented acceptance date, (3) acknowledgment of review cadence (annual), (4) acknowledgment of reactivation criteria. This can be resolved in any governance session (700-series) — no 600-series activation is required.
c_005_governance_board_not_accepted.blocking_rationale: GATE_BOARD requires the Governance Board to hold an activation vote. Until the Governance Board accepts stewardship, there is no authorized entity to hold the vote.

summary.open_label: C-005: Governance Board acceptance of S725 Row 16 — can be resolved by Governance Board now, no 600 activation needed
summary.carry_forward_label: C-001 (800 handoff) + C-002 (700 authority drift) — must be resolved during activation review
summary.accepted_label: C-003 (registry maintenance tension) + C-004 (analytics consumption boundary) — LOW severity, accepted as non-blocking
summary.blocking_label: C-001, C-002, C-005 — all 3 must be resolved before GATE_OWNERSHIP or GATE_BOARD can pass

recommendation: The Governance Board should resolve C-005 (GAP-3 acceptance) in the next governance session — this is the only conflict that can be resolved without 600 activation. C-001 and C-002 are correctly classified as CARRY_FORWARD — they are documented, understood, and will be resolved during activation review as part of GATE_OWNERSHIP satisfaction. C-003 and C-004 are correctly classified as ACCEPTED — they are LOW severity procedural notes with well-defined boundaries. The ownership conflict landscape is stable for the DEFERRED state.
